title: Upper Airway & Larynx Anatomy: Cartilages & Vocal Folds
description: Learn upper airway and larynx anatomy from the nasal conchae and three pharyngeal regions to the epiglottis, laryngeal cartilages, vocal folds, and airway.
h1: Upper Airway and Larynx Anatomy: Pharynx, Cartilages and Vocal Folds
blurb: Warming nasal conchae, the three-part pharynx, and the nine cartilages of the larynx that protect the lower airway during swallowing and vibrate vocal folds.
lead: At the crossroads of breathing and swallowing, the upper airway warms and filters inspired air while the cartilaginous larynx guards the lungs and generates the human voice. This illustrated study guide examines 20 documented anatomical entries—including Nasal cavity & conchae, Paranasal sinuses, Nasopharynx & adenoid—connecting visible form, tissue organization, and physiological function.

Midsagittal cut from nasal conchae to tracheal rings — including the parts you cannot see from outside: sinuses, adenoid, vocal folds.

When you trace how upper airway and larynx anatomy functions in the living body, each documented landmark contributes a specific mechanical or physiological step. Key structures covered in this guide include Nasal cavity & conchae (warms, humidifies and filters inspired air), Paranasal sinuses (lighten the skull; resonate voice; humidify), Nasopharynx & adenoid (air passage; immune sampling in childhood), and Oropharynx (shared food–air corridor; speech resonance). By following all 20 illustrated landmarks in sequence, you can see how gross morphology, internal chambers or layers, and surrounding vessels work as one integrated unit.

Understanding these structural relationships is essential for both anatomy exams and real-world physiological reasoning. Practical anatomical correlations also stand out: for nasal cavity & conchae, deviated septum + turbinate hypertrophy = blocked nose; for paranasal sinuses, sinusitis pain follows the sinus walls — maxillary = cheekache. questions.question: What is the path of air through the upper airway?
questions.answer: Air enters the nose or mouth, passes through the pharynx and larynx, then moves down the trachea toward the bronchi. In relation to epiglottis, this structure flips to cover the larynx during swallowing. From an anatomical and functional standpoint, epiglottitis: drooling, stridor — an airway emergency.

questions.question: What does the epiglottis do during swallowing?
questions.answer: The epiglottis is one structure involved in protecting the laryngeal entrance during swallowing; coordinated movement of the larynx and vocal folds also matters. From an anatomical and functional standpoint, epiglottitis: drooling, stridor — an airway emergency.
